x: Manigramam was a guild engaged in foreign or long-distance trade.
tq: Discriminate between long-distance trading guilds and local merchant assemblies.

s: The Ainnurruvar, known as the ‘Five Hundred’ of Ayyavole, was a
o: royal council concerned with temple architecture
powerful inter-regional and overseas merchant body
guild of Arab horse traders alone
x: The Ainnurruvar was a powerful inter-regional and overseas merchant body.
tq: Use the scale of activity—inter-regional and overseas—to identify the guild.

s: The name ‘Nanadesis’ most closely indicates merchants ‘of’
x: Nanadesis means merchants ‘of many countries’ and was associated with foreign trade.
tq: Use the literal qualification in the guild name to distinguish foreign traders from local assemblies.

s: What was the principal activity of the Nagaram?
o: Local merchant assembly and domestic trade in market towns
x: Nagaram was a local merchant assembly in market towns and was associated with domestic trade.
tq: Separate the local domestic role of Nagaram from the overseas role of other guilds.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Guild or body)
a. Manigramam
b. Ainnurruvar
c. Nanadesis
 d. Nagaram

List-II (Activity)
i. Local merchant assembly and domestic trade
 ii. Foreign or long-distance trade
 iii. Inter-regional and overseas trade
 iv. Foreign trade, meaning ‘of many countries’

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Manigramam handled foreign or long-distance trade; Ainnurruvar was inter-regional and overseas; Nanadesis represented merchants of many countries; Nagaram was local and domestic.
tq: Build the answer from the distinctive sure pair Nagaram–local domestic trade, then verify the remaining guilds.

s: As Chola power declined, the merchant guilds
o: became independent and adopted their own codes and collective decisions
were abolished by the royal administration
restricted themselves exclusively to temple donations
lost all role in foreign trade
x: With the waning of Chola power, the guilds grew independent and developed their own codes of conduct and collective decision-making.
tq: Identify the institutional change associated with the decline of central power.

s: In Andhra, the Nanadesi Pekkundru and the Nakaram were respectively associated with
x: The Nanadesi Pekkundru was the foreign-trade guild in Andhra, while the Nakaram was associated with domestic trade.
tq: Test the reversed roles of the two Andhra merchant bodies.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nakaram — Overseas merchant body in Andhra
Nanadesi Pekkundru — Foreign trade in Andhra
Ainnurruvar — Inter-regional and overseas merchant body
x: Nakaram was the domestic-trade body in Andhra, whereas Nanadesi Pekkundru was associated with foreign trade.
tq: Look for the reversed foreign–domestic distinction in the Andhra guild pair.

s: The Anaimangalam copper plates are presently associated with which institution?
x: The Chola-era Anaimangalam copper plates were held by Leiden University for almost two centuries.
tq: Identify the present institutional custodian in a current-affairs heritage question.

s: The Anaimangalam copper plates were returned to India by the Netherlands in
x: The Anaimangalam copper plates were returned by the Netherlands in May 2026, specifically on 16 May 2026.
tq: Distinguish the precise return year from nearby current-affairs dates.

s: The Anaimangalam copper plates document Chola links with Srivijaya in the spheres of
x: The plates document Chola–Srivijaya religious and trade links.
tq: Match the inscriptional source with the two domains explicitly documented by it.

s: The Kudavolai system was cited as evidence of
o: the beginning of Roman trade in India
x: The Chola Kudavolai ballot-pot system was cited as proof of early Indian democracy.
tq: Recognise the institutional function of a historical voting method in a contemporary reference.

s: Rajendra I was highlighted as the builder of
x: Rajendra I, whose reign is given as 1012–1044, was highlighted as the builder of Gangaikondacholapuram.
tq: Match the ruler and regnal period with the city associated with his architectural legacy.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to architectural styles in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Draksharama Bhimeswara — exclusively Imperial Chola style
x: Draksharama Bhimeswara represents the independent Chalukya-Chola style. Brihadeeswara is Imperial Chola, while Padmakshi at Hanamkonda is Kakatiya.
tq: Use the regional architectural comparisons to reject swapped dynastic styles.

s: The independent Chalukya-Chola style of the Draksharama Bhimeswara temple reflects the combination of
x: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple shows an independent Chalukya-Chola style combining Pallava and early Chalukya elements.
tq: Identify the component traditions behind a named regional architectural style.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the comparative development of Dravidian art?
o: The Pallavas laid its foundation and the Cholas developed it on a monumental scale.
The Cholas laid its foundation and the Pallavas built its monumental culmination.
The Rashtrakutas alone created the Dravidian tradition.
The Hoysalas laid its foundation and the Kakatiyas completed it.
x: The comparison states that the Pallavas laid the foundation of Dravidian art, while the Cholas built its monumental culmination.
tq: Preserve the direction of the comparison instead of reversing the contributions of the Pallavas and Cholas.

s: The third phase of underwater exploration mentioned in connection with Poompuhar was begun by
x: Tamil Nadu began the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar or Kaveripattinam.
tq: Identify the state undertaking the current archaeological exploration.

s:
Earlier underwater finds at Poompuhar included which of the following?
1. Wharves
2. Fourth-century BCE pottery
3. A lighthouse
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Earlier finds at Poompuhar included wharves, fourth-century BCE pottery and a lighthouse.
tq: Check all three archaeological discoveries before selecting the complete combination.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Angkor Wat — a monument of the Imperial Chola style in Tamil Nadu
x: Angkor Wat is an example of South-East Asian architecture influenced by the wider transmission of Dravidian art; it is not a monument of Imperial Chola style located in Tamil Nadu.
tq: Reject the option that turns cultural influence into an incorrect location and dynastic attribution.
